merged_comments.content: start() and stop() mutate `job` and `gateToken` with no common lock (`job` is not even @Volatile), so the sequence `tryAcquire() -> gateToken = token -> job = launch(...)` is not atomic with respect to a concurrent stop(). OnceGate only serializes the gate acquire, not these surrounding field writes. Failure modes: (a) stop() lands between tryAcquire() and the assignments -> it reads null/stale values, cancels nothing, and returns while the just-started read loop keeps capturing forever (lost stop: mic stays open, gate held so future start() silently no-ops); (b) stop() reads gateToken just after start() stored it but before/around job assignment -> it releases the gate while the read loop it meant to stop is still alive, so the next start() acquires the gate and runs a SECOND capture loop in parallel, double-feeding stampedBlocks and fighting over the mic. Serialize start/stop on one lock and let stop() hand the token to the job's completion instead of releasing immediately (also fixes the early-release overlap below).

stop() frees the gate immediately, but cancellation is cooperative: the read loop may still be blocked inside r.read() for up to one 100ms block before its finally runs r.stop()/r.release(). An immediate start() then acquires the freed gate and builds a fresh AudioRecord while the mic is still held by the old one; on devices with exclusive mic access both source candidates fail, buildRecord() just logs the error and capture silently never starts (isRunning stays false). Release the gate only when the old job has actually finished (e.g. `j?.invokeOnCompletion { token?.let(startGate::release) }` after cancel — this also covers the 'coroutine cancelled before its body ran' case this fallback currently handles), or join/cancelAndJoin the old job before building the new record.

The error code returned by startRecording() is ignored, so isRunning is set to true even when the device refuses to start (degraded state / HAL error). Consumers then see a healthy-looking capture while the read loop spins on persistent error returns (compounding the pumpBlocks busy-spin), and diagnostics are misled. Check the returned error code (and recordingState == RECORDSTATE_RECORDING) and bail out on failure — the finally already releases the AudioRecord and the coroutine finally releases the gate, unblocking a clean restart.

merged_comments.content: Uncaught exceptions can crash the process, contradicting both the class KDoc ("任何一步落空即退，不让异常逃出线程", "失败全程静默…任何失败不劣于现状") and the finally-guard comment. Only ttsSynthesize and cacheStore.write are wrapped; resolver.snapshot(), WakeAckSelector.needsPrefetch/cacheKey/fileName, WakeAckAudio.validate/process/toSamples, and WavCodec.pcmToWav are unguarded — any exception they throw propagates to the thread's default uncaught handler and kills the app (the status-quo fallback path never crashes). Additionally the two guarded regions catch only Exception, so an OutOfMemoryError from allocating large PCM buffers inside synthOk also escapes. Fix: wrap the entire run() body in one try/catch(Exception) that logs via PetLogger (and records backoff when key is available), instead of scattering per-call guards.

TOCTOU race between cache key and synthesized voice: key is derived from resolver.snapshot() at run() start, but ttsSynthesize(app, TEXT) leaves voice="default", so the actual timbre is read from live NetConfig inside CloudClientFactory at call time (per the class KDoc: "aliyun/volc 分支直接读 NetConfig"). If the user saves a new voice between snapshot() and this call, the NEW voice's audio gets written atomically under the OLD config's fileName — later reverting to the old tuple would play wrong-voice audio from cache, breaking the key↔audio invariant the comment claims ("key/fileName 用 selector 同一函数，与播放侧对账"). Fix: pass the snapshot's voice explicitly (CloudClientFactory.ttsSynthesize(app, TtsVoiceDefaults.TEXT, voice = snap.voice)), or re-snapshot after synthesis and skip storing when the key changed.

Triggers arriving while a run is in flight are silently dropped: CAS fails and maybePrefetch returns without recording that work is owed. Since run() freezes the snapshot/cache key at start and synthesis+disk write can take seconds, a config saved during that window is never prefetched — the dropped caller's config stays uncached until the next unrelated trigger (session assembly or another save). The fallback chain masks it (vendor asset plays), but the "保存即合成 + 启动补漏" guarantee silently degrades. Fix: set a pending flag before the CAS-return and have the daemon re-check/re-run once at the end of run() with a fresh snapshot, so the latest saved config always gets prefetched.

merged_comments.content: Hand-rolled Thread(...).apply { isDaemon = true; start() } is verbose and bypasses structured exception handling: an escaping throw (see the unguarded-steps issue) goes to the process default handler with no chance to log/route. Prefer kotlin.concurrent.thread(name = ..., isDaemon = true) { ... } for conciseness, and/or setUncaughtExceptionHandler (or a single-thread executor / supervised coroutine) so cold-path failures are logged rather than crashing — consistent with the "后台补漏不该打扰用户" contract.

Data race: this unsynchronized ArrayDeque is mutated from two concurrency domains. In VoiceSessionManager, add()/drain() run on the capture-collect coroutine (Dispatchers.Default), but clear() is invoked from playAckThenListen() and cancelCurrentTurn(), which are reachable from the KWS wake-callback thread and UI/barge-in threads — the documented 'wake-interrupt-wake during ack playback' scenario executes wakeBlindBuffer.add() on the collect loop while clear() runs on another thread. kotlin.collections.ArrayDeque is not thread-safe: a concurrent clear()/addLast() can lose entries, corrupt head/tail indices, or throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Additionally, drainEntries()' toList-then-clear is non-atomic, so a block added between the two steps is silently dropped, breaking the documented 'backfill exactly once, no audio loss' contract. The codebase already established the fix pattern for exactly this consume-thread vs cross-thread-cleanup race (see VoiceSessionManager.continuationLock). Synchronize all accessors on a private lock.

merged_comments.content: Memo caches fallback/NONE outcomes under the outer Decision with no invalidation, so transient failures become permanent for the process lifetime (the resolver is a process-lifetime singleton in VoiceClientFactory). Concrete scenarios: (1) cache file passes exists() but read/strip fails once -> selectAndLoad falls back to the asset layer and memo[PlayCache] stores the asset bytes; after prefetch later repairs/rewrites the cache, the Decision key is unchanged, so memo[decision] hits forever and the good cache is never re-read. (2) A single transient IOException in assetReader memoizes the platform fallback (or NONE) under PlayAsset(vendor); the vendor asset is never retried again. (3) A memoized NONE keeps resolve() returning null until config changes or process restart. Fix: only memoize results that came from the selected layer itself (skip the memo write — or evict the entry — whenever a fallback was taken), or key the memo by a freshness signal (e.g. cache file length/lastModified) so repaired files are picked up.

assetNames() memoizes the first assetLister() result for the instance lifetime, but the production assetLister in from() swallows IOException into an empty set (runCatching...getOrDefault(emptyArray())). One transient assets.list failure therefore permanently (process lifetime) and silently disables every vendor-asset layer of the fallback chain (isBundledDefault branch and layer 4 in WakeAckSelector.select), degrading wake-ack to cache/platform with zero diagnostics — and it can never self-heal. Fix: don't memoize empty results so the next resolve() retries, and log the lister failure in from() to preserve the S9-4 forensic chain.
